verified_facts: OS NGD Water separates topographic Water Features from the structured Water Network collection
theme, collection and feature-type identity must be retained
OS NGD Water has distinct Water Features and Water Network collections
collection terminology controls access and schema interpretation
Water Features is the topographic collection and is distinct from the network model
feature geometry roles must not be inferred from the network collection
Water Network is a three-dimensional structured link-and-node network for Great Britain
feature types are Water Link, Water Node and Water Link Set
updates are quarterly and persistent identifiers with lifecycle information are supplied
Water Link and Water Node default to EPSG:7405 while Water Link Set defaults to EPSG:27700
Water Link models general alignment and connectivity of permanent water
permanence, capture specification, level of detail, catchment and width fields have separate semantics
catchment and width fields can legitimately be null
minimum and maximum width are calculated only for links derived from polygon water
Water Node is a point where connected permanent water ends, joins or changes attribution
schema 1.1 launched 28 October 2025 and added Tidal Outlet
temporal snapshots earlier than 29 September 2022 may be inconsistent
Water Link Set represents an accepted named body of water through which the network flows
a cross-reference links Water Link Set and Water Link features
temporal snapshots earlier than 29 September 2022 may be inconsistent
the product is a three-dimensional structured link-and-node network
obscured or underground connectivity can be inferred from accepted sources
water polygons and banks remain in OS MasterMap Topography rather than this network product
WatercourseLink is a segment representing watercourse alignment
centreline geometry is mandatory
classification or name changes split links and may create a pseudo node
HydroNode exists at WatercourseLink endpoints and records starts, ends, junctions or attribution changes
positions are three-dimensional and vertical coordinates come from OS terrain data
OS Open Rivers is a two-dimensional generalized link-and-node network for Great Britain
links are digitised in water-flow direction
the product is automatically generalized from large-scale data
Open Rivers WatercourseLink is a generalized watercourse alignment
flow direction and link length have explicit roles
the theme contains administrative, legislative, statistical, governance and service-delivery extents
OSIDs are supplied even for several boundary types without GSS codes or TOIDs
Boundaries covers Great Britain with EPSG:27700 default CRS
parent references, land area, tidal area, total area and detached-part flags have distinct meanings
the collection is available through Select+Build and Tiles rather than the NGD Features API
Boundary High Water Mark represents mean high water springs to the normal tidal limit
it is an administrative-boundary feature and not a cadastral parcel edge
Ward is a voting subdivision of a higher feature
temporal snapshots earlier than 29 September 2022 may be inconsistent
GSS codes must be interpreted as boundary identifiers rather than property identifiers
matching may use postcode with the November 2025 NSPL or UPRN with the November 2025 ONS UPRN Directory
current_gigabit and future_gigabit derive from BDUK OMR and delivery evidence and carry epoch limitations
absence from the release is not proof that a premises lacks connectivity
the publication is dated 4 June 2026 and applies to England and Wales
sample and regional archives are separate release assets
planned deployment outputs use the Spring 2026 premise base
residential and all-premises outputs have different denominators
High Confidence plans are distinct from all reported plans
fixed and mobile downloads are separate
fixed coverage contains maximum available speeds while postcode fixed-performance files are no longer produced from 2024
